title: fix(plugin-security): the delegated-admin gate resolves a position name inside the caller's own organization
body:
Closes #19819

Clause-②: no

The delegated-administration gate resolved `sys_position` **by NAME across organizations** in the two reads that decide authority over a position: whether it may be self-delegated (ADR-0091 D3 rule 5) and which permission sets it distributes (the delegated-assignment allowlist and containment checks, D3 rule 6, and the `assignablePositions` list of `describeDelegableScope`). This PR scopes both to the caller's own organization with the shape the business-unit anchor read in the same file already uses since `a5afe382ba`.

## The defect, verified at source before the repair

On `origin/main` at the branch point `afc3b64928`, `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/delegated-admin-gate.ts`:

- `positionIsDelegatable` and `setsBoundToPosition` both did `ql.find('sys_position', { where: { name: positionName }, limit: 1, context: SYSTEM_CTX })`. `SYSTEM_CTX` is `{ isSystem: true }` and carries no tenant, so the driver applied no organization predicate.
- `sys_position` is a per-organization catalog upserted by `(name, organization_id)` and `name` carries no installation-wide uniqueness, so `limit: 1` answered whichever id the SQL driver ordered first.

## Measured: yes, the crossing was an escalation (triage asked this first)

The triage comment asked whether an org X delegate could (a) self-delegate a position because org Y's same-named row is delegatable, or (b) hand out a set bound only through Y's row. Measured on a real `ObjectQL` over a real `SqlDriver` (in-memory SQLite), with the other organization's ids sorting first: **both happened.**

- (a) An org A holder **self-delegated `field_lead`, which org A marked NOT delegatable**, because org B's row was delegatable: the gate resolved where it should refuse.
- (b) An org A delegate whose scope allowlists only `sales_user` was **approved to assign `closer`, whose org A binding distributes `finance_user`**, because org B's `closer` binds `sales_user`. Org B's bindings were the ones checked.
- The reverse also held: org A was refused positions its own bindings allow, and D3 rule 6 read org B's admin set against org A.

Caveat on reach: the test orders ids on purpose. Whether a real deployment's id generation puts the other organization's row first is not measured here. The outcome depends on id ordering, not on any design guarantee.

## The repair

- A new private helper, `resolveOwnPosition(positionName, organizationId)`, is the one read both decisions use. It keeps both arms of the business-unit repair, and each arm is measured below. (1) The read carries `organizationScopedCtx(organizationId)`, so the driver adds a tenant predicate. (2) `resolveOwnOrganizationRow(...).own` keeps only the caller's own row from what comes back. The driver's compatibility arm also returns organization-less rows, and a driver with no tenant scoping returns every organization's rows. The candidate page is `ANCHOR_CANDIDATE_LIMIT` rather than `1`, for the same reason as the anchor read.
- `positionIsDelegatable` and `setsBoundToPosition` take the caller's `organizationId`. It is threaded from `assert()` (`callerOrganizationId(ctx)`, the same value the anchor read already used) into `assertSelfDelegation` and `assertAssignmentWrite`, and from `describeDelegableScope`'s `callerContext`. Once the row is resolved, bindings and sets are read by that row's id, which no other organization shares.
- **Fail closed**: a position name with no row in the caller's organization is not delegatable and distributes no permission sets. It never falls back to another organization's row or to an unscoped read. Under a walled posture an organization-less `sys_position` row no longer answers either question, because that posture already treats such a row as invalid state.
- **Unchanged where there is no boundary to cross**: a caller with no organization (the `single` posture) keeps the by-name answer, and its own test pins this.
- No exported symbol, payload key, error code or refusal message is added or changed. Zero lines in `packages/spec`.

## Evidence

Two complementary suites, as in the business-unit repair:

- `delegated-admin-gate-position-organization.test.ts` (new, real engine) has one witness block per read. Each block uses two organizations, the same position name and different answers, and asserts that each organization sees only its own answer. It also has the no-row-in-my-org case for each read and two controls: a single organization, and a caller with no organization.
- `delegated-admin-gate.test.ts` gains a companion block on the existing context-ignoring double: a driver with no tenant scoping, plus an organization-less residue row. There the row-level arm is the only thing standing.

**BEFORE**: only the gate source reverted to `afc3b64928`, proved on disk by blob hash (`732cc64311b9…` = the base blob, `resolveOwnPosition` count 0). The new test file was kept:

```
$ pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-security exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/delegated-admin-gate-position-organization.test.ts
 × org A, which did NOT opt in, refuses the self-delegation — org B's opt-in does not answer for it
     AssertionError: promise resolved "undefined" instead of rejecting
 × a position with NO row in the caller's organization is not delegatable (fail closed)
     AssertionError: promise resolved "undefined" instead of rejecting
 × org A judges `lead` by its OWN binding (allowlisted) — approved
     AssertionError: promise rejected "PermissionDeniedError: …" instead of resolving
 × org A judges `closer` by its OWN binding (not allowlisted) — refused, org B's binding does not launder it
     AssertionError: promise resolved "undefined" instead of rejecting
 × describeDelegableScope offers each organization only the positions its OWN bindings allow
     AssertionError: expected [ 'closer' ] to deeply equal [ 'lead' ]
 × self-delegation rule 6 reads the caller's own bindings — an admin set bound only in org B does not block org A
 × a position with NO row in the caller's organization distributes no sets — org B's bindings never judge org A
 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  7 failed | 5 passed (12)
```

The 5 that passed are the ground-truth read, the two org B cases (org B's row sorts first, so the old read happened to be right for it), and the two controls.

**AFTER**: the source was restored with `git checkout HEAD -- …`. The restore is proved by `git hash-object` = HEAD blob `dabd229755d7…` and an empty `git diff HEAD`. Result: `Test Files 3 passed (3) · Tests 84 passed (84)` across the new file, `delegated-admin-gate.test.ts` and `delegated-admin-gate-cross-organization.test.ts`.

**ABLATION (row-level arm)**: `node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs --hold` replaced `resolveOwnOrganizationRow(…).own` in `resolveOwnPosition` with `rows[0] ?? null`. Anchor count went 1 → 0, replacement count 0 → 1, blob `dabd229755d7` → `2ea8e472c017`:

```
 × refuses a self-delegation org A never opted in to, whatever org B's first row says
 × an organization-less residue row does not make a position delegatable for a walled caller
 × judges a delegated assignment by org A's own bindings, not org B's first row
 Test Files  1 failed | 1 passed (2)
      Tests  3 failed | 76 passed (79)
```

The context-ignoring half went red and the real-engine half stayed green. That is the split the code comment claims, so neither arm is decoration. `--restore` then reported blob == HEAD and `git diff HEAD` empty. The tests import the gate from `src/`, so no `dist/` is in the resolution path.

## Verification (all readings at `0b3e2d7aae`, the final commit)

|:--|:--|:--|
| dependency closure | `pnpm --filter '@objectstack/plugin-security^...' build` | exit 0 |
| package tests | `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-security test` | 119 files / **2277 passed** |
| package typecheck | `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-security typecheck` | exit 0, test layer 0 errors |
| derived gate families | `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands`, then `--ran` with exit codes | **62 derived, 62 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED** |
| lint (narrowed) | `pnpm exec eslint --no-inline-config --format json` on the 3 touched `.ts` files | 3 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings |

Three gate families first answered `PREREQUISITE NOT MET` (exit 3, not a finding) because they read built output: `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:i18n` and `check:type-check-debt`. All three are green after `turbo run build --filter=./packages/* --filter=./packages/*/*` (72/72 successful).

Lint was narrowed rather than whole-tree. The narrowing rests on three facts. (1) The population comes from eslint's own config: the three files match `**/*.{ts,…}` and `--print-config` resolves a config for them, so none is ignored. (2) The file count comes from the JSON output: 3 files. (3) `eslint.config.mjs` enables no type-aware linting (no `parserOptions.project`; `--print-config` reports `project: null`), so this diff cannot change the verdict on any untouched file. CI runs the whole-tree `pnpm lint`.

Not run here and left to CI: the path-scheduled CI jobs, the whole-workspace type-check lanes and the artifact-roster families.

## Acceptance notes

Observed while reading the fix, deliberately **not** changed here:

- **The card's boundary note is right for `businessUnitsOfUser` and not quite right for `assignmentAnchorsOfPosition`.** The latter reads `sys_user_position` by `{ position: positionName }` under `SYSTEM_CTX`. That is a position name, not a globally unique id, so another organization's assignments of a same-named position enter a binding write's blast-radius set. Their anchors lie outside the caller's subtree, so the observed direction is over-refusal (fail closed) and not a widening. It was left alone per the dispatch.
- **`activeHoldings` (self-delegation rule 4) crosses organizations too, and this PR does not repair it.** It reads `sys_user_position` by `(user_id, position name)` under `SYSTEM_CTX`. A throwaway probe on this branch's head (real engine, not committed) measured the result. A user whose only direct `field_lead` holding is stamped for org B was **approved** to self-delegate org A's `field_lead` (delegatable in org A) while acting in org A. Rule 4's "you currently hold it" was answered by the other organization's row. This is not fixed in place because the repair shape is not pinned. The runtime resolver keeps organization-less `sys_user_position` rows for any tenant (`resolve-authz-context.ts`), so "own row only" (this PR's shape) and "not another organization's row" are different repairs. That choice belongs on its own card, which is handed back to the seat.
- The runtime resolver (`packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts`) reads position-bound sets through the caller's tenant. The gate's "no row in my organization distributes nothing" answer therefore agrees with what an assignment actually grants.
